column3: NASB renders “were delivering” as “proceeded to deliver” and “cohort of Augustus” as “Augustan cohort.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “the coast of” and renders “set sail” as “put out to sea.”
NASB follows the critical text; “landed” is rendered “put in,” and “considerately” is “with consideration.”
NASB adds “the shelter of.”
NASB adds “the coast of” and renders “came” as “landed.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “many days” as “a good many days” and adds “to go farther” and “the shelter of.”
NASB renders “coasting along” as “sailing past.”
NASB renders “was admonishing” as “began to admonish”; “the Fast” is lowercase.
NASB follows the critical text (“cargo”); “with disaster” is rendered “attended with damage,” and it adds “certainly.”
NASB follows the critical text; “the ship owner” is rendered “the captain of the ship.”
NASB follows the critical text and reorders the verse, moving “to winter there” to the end.
NASB renders “was blowing gently” as “a moderate south wind came up” and “very near” as “close inshore.”
NASB renders “from it” as “from the land” and transliterates the wind's name as “Euraquilo.”
NASB adds “to it” and “let ourselves.”
NASB reads “Clauda,” the spelling of other manuscripts; the critical text has “Cauda.” “Lifeboat” is rendered “ship's boat.”
NASB renders “supports” as “supporting cables” and “the gear” as “the sea anchor.”
NASB renders “were making a jettison” as “began to jettison.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB renders “was abandoned” as “was gradually abandoned.”
NASB follows the critical text; “having been obedient to me” is rendered “followed my advice.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “this night” as “this very night” and “stood by” as “stood before.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “take courage” as “keep up your courage” and adds “exactly.”
NASB renders “fall upon” as “run aground on.”
NASB renders “the Adriatic” as “the Adriatic Sea” and “were sensing” as “began to surmise.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; “were praying” is rendered “wished.”
NASB renders “lifeboat” as “ship's boat” and “cast out” as “lay out.”
